statement: For maximum clique on graphs with N<=1000, a hybrid approach combining BnB (degeneracy ordering + greedy coloring bound with bitset color classes) with DLS tabu search fallback achieves optimal solutions within 2s, whereas pure BnB plateaus around 88-90% on hard dense instances.
regime: N <= 1000, M <= 500000, time limit 2s, undirected graphs
mechanism: BnB with degeneracy ordering focuses search on the densest core first. Bitset color classes provide O(N/64) adjacency checks for coloring. When BnB times out on hard dense instances, DLS tabu search escapes local optima by systematically removing/adding clique vertices with tabu-based diversification, finding the optimal clique heuristically.
applicability_bounds: Applies to maximum clique on moderate-size graphs. For N >> 1000 or very dense graphs, the BnB component may contribute less and local search becomes dominant.

statement: Greedy clique construction by degree descending finds only ~34% of optimal clique size on average for the test suite, confirming that exhaustive search or sophisticated local search is essential for near-optimal max clique.
mechanism: Greedy selection gets stuck in local optima: high-degree vertices are chosen first but may not participate in the maximum clique. Without backtracking or swapping, the greedy solution is far from optimal.
applicability_bounds: The 34% ratio depends on the specific test instance mix. For easy instances (sparse graphs or graphs where the max clique is small), greedy may perform better.
